answer: I'd like to talk about a decision that honestly kept me awake at night for weeks. One of the hardest decisions I have faced was turning down a stable job to pursue something more uncertain but closer to what I actually wanted. This was about two years ago, just after I had been offered a comfortable position with good pay at a bank, only a few months after finishing my BBA. At the same time, a small education consultancy offered me a role helping students apply to study abroad, which paid less but felt far more meaningful. On paper the bank was the sensible choice, which is exactly what made walking away so [[agonising]]. In my town, a bank job is seen as a real achievement, so I knew people would question my judgement. I spent weeks weighing it up, going back and forth, because the secure option felt safe while the other was a genuine [[gamble]]. What ultimately tipped the balance was realising I would probably [[bitterly regret]] not taking the risk far more than any short-term setback. Telling my family was nerve-wracking, since they naturally worried, but they came round once they saw how [[determined]] I was. As for how I felt, I was anxious for a long time, but also strangely [[liberated]]. Looking back, it was a real turning point, and although the following months were rocky, it taught me that the most rewarding paths are rarely the most comfortable. I still feel it was the right call.

followUps.q: Did your family agree with your decision in the end?
followUps.answer: Yes, eventually. My father was the first to support me, probably because he ran his own business for over thirty years and understood taking a chance. My mother took a little longer to feel comfortable.

followUps.q: Do you find it easy to make decisions in general?
followUps.answer: Not really, to be honest. For small things I'm quick, but with big decisions I tend to overthink. These days I try to set myself a deadline so I don't go round in circles forever.
